sources.source: Safety in Custody Statistics: deaths to March 2026; assaults and self-harm to December 2025
sources.authority: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.verified_fact: The accredited release records 352 deaths in prison custody in the 12 months to March 2026, including 67 self-inflicted deaths. For the 12 months to December 2025 it records 72,753 self-harm incidents and 31,345 assaults.
sources.quality_effect: Adds adult-custody safety context while requiring rates per 1,000 prisoners, rolling-period alignment, population-change adjustment and later cause-of-death revision guards; custody incidents are not neighbourhood or parcel risk.

sources.source: Safety in the Children and Young People Secure Estate: update to December 2025
sources.authority: Ministry of Justice, HM Prison and Probation Service and Youth Custody Service
sources.verified_fact: The official release records 489 assault incidents and 400 self-harm incidents in October to December 2025, involving 318 unique assailants or fighters and 78 unique children or young people who self-harmed. No death was reported in the year to December 2025.
sources.quality_effect: Adds secure-estate safeguarding context with small-population volatility, repeated-incident, sector-model, annualised-rate and temporarily closed Secure School exclusion guards.

sources.authority: Youth Justice Board for England and Wales
sources.verified_fact: The accredited annual report records about 58,300 arrests of children, just over 8,100 first-time entrants, about 35,600 proven offences and an average of just under 420 children aged 10 to 17 in custody, using different reference periods where specified.
sources.quality_effect: Adds youth-justice flow context while preserving multi-source, age-definition, reference-period, rounding, revised offence-group and administrative-outcome guards; arrests, cautions, proven offences and custody are distinct units.

sources.source: Police powers and procedures: stop and search, arrests and mental health detentions, year ending March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The accredited release records 528,582 stop and searches under all relevant legislation, a 14.9% resultant-arrest rate and 754,046 arrests in the year ending March 2025.
sources.quality_effect: Adds police-powers activity context while separating searches, resultant arrests and all arrests, and retaining legislation, police-force, population-rate and pre-2010 British Transport Police coverage limits.

sources.authority: HM Prison and Probation Service and Youth Custody Service
sources.verified_fact: The official monthly collection was updated on 10 July 2026 with May 2026 data and covers the population aged 10 to 18+ across secure children's homes, Oasis Restore Secure School, secure training centres and young offender institutions, including legal basis and distance from home.
sources.quality_effect: Adds a current secure-estate population snapshot with month-end, age-scope, establishment-sector, placement and distance-from-home guards; it is not an incident series or local public-safety prevalence measure.

sources.source: Electronic Monitoring Statistics Publication, England and Wales: June 2026
sources.verified_fact: The official release records 27,847 individuals assigned with electronic-monitoring equipment at 30 June 2026, 3% below March 2026. The publication attributes the decrease mainly to a June data cleanse that closed expired or non-communicating orders.
sources.quality_effect: Adds supervision-service context with equipment-assignment, multiple-order, cohort, data-cleanse and methodology-break guards; the decline cannot be interpreted as a comparable fall in monitored risk or offending.

sources.source: Deaths of offenders in the community, annual update to March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The official release records 1,413 deaths among people supervised in the community in 2024/25: 1,233 male and 180 female deaths. Of the total, 752 occurred while serving court orders and 620 under post-release supervision.
sources.quality_effect: Adds probation-supervision safeguarding context while retaining supervision-status, caseload-size, Offender Rehabilitation Act expansion, cause-classification and person-period guards; counts are not community mortality rates or parcel risk.
